chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar narrated to us, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):

I heard Hisham ibn al-Hakam narrating from you that Allah, the Mighty and High, is a body, solid, luminous; His recognition is necessary, which He bestows upon whom He wills from His creation. He (peace be upon him) said: Glory to Him whom no one knows how He is except Himself. There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing. He is not bounded, nor sensed, nor corporeal, nor tangible, and the senses do not perceive Him. Nothing encompasses Him. He is not a body, nor an image, nor lineation, nor delineation.

key_terms.لَا تَدْرِكُهُ ٱلْحَوَاسُّ: The senses do not perceive Him
key_terms.لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِۦ شَيْءٌ: There is nothing like unto Him

ai.seo_question: What are the divine attributes of Allah regarding body and form according to Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* articulates the core Shia doctrine of *Tanzih* (divine transcendence) by refuting the *Jismiyah* (corporealism) school, which posited that God possesses a physical body. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) systematically negates all sensory attributes—limitation, perception, and touch—to establish that Allah is devoid of *Jism* (body) and *Surah* (form), relying on the Quranic maxim 'There is nothing like unto Him' to affirm His absolute incomparability.
